objective: Proof: starts whose knots share no neighbour split into independent pieces; under one count two first knots grow together exactly when their open distinctions agree (apart: equal sizes; sharing one distinction: equal sizes, one fewer each), so no size wins; under the fewest counts a lone knot closes and two knots sharing one distinction grow two-dimensionally for every pair of sizes.
status: Proved 2026-11-18 (referee pending): a start of knots sharing no neighbour grows as independent pieces, each a seed on its open distinctions, so the rule never sees a size (Lemma 1); one count runs exactly when every start knot has 0, 1 or c open distinctions, so a three-place and a four-place first knot apart or touching once cannot grow under any count (Theorem 2); the same relation grows at count 4 or 2 by presentation (Corollary 2.1); the fewest counts close separate knots and grow two touching knots as two copies of N^2, exactly, for every pair of sizes, through a relay of the touching distinction (Theorem 3); m mutually touching knots of m + 1 places grow m-dimensionally under the fewest counts (Proposition 4, after the census).
title: Two first knots under one count and under the fewest counts
